content.text: : 6-8wk period following birth in which the reproductive tract, as well as the rest of the body, returns to the nonpregnant state
recommended for women w/ uncomplicated pregnancies & deliveries
immediately after delivery the fundus of the uterus is palpable halfway between the pubic symphysis & umbilicus
– immediate size reduction results from delivery of fetus, placenta, & amniotic fluid
– as a result of these changes, the
uterus returns to the pelvis by 2wks postpartum & to its normal size by 6wks postpartum
contraction of the smooth muscle of the arterial walls
compression of the vasculature by the uterine musculature
blood clots from the uterus are expelled
in the large vessels of the placental bed
adjacent to the myometrium, which had contained the fundi of the endometrial glands – the
basal layer is the source of the new endometrium
– fairly heavy at first & rapidly ↓ in amount over the first 2-3d postpartum (may last for several weeks)
in the first several days, consisting mainly of
lighter discharge w/ considerably less blood
that may persist for several weeks – may be misunderstood as illness by some women, requiring explanation & reassurance
Lochia resolves more quickly in women who breastfeed
– possible d/t more rapid involution of the uterus caused by uterine contractions associated w/ breastfeeding
*By the end of the 3rdwk postpartum, the endometrium is reestablished in most pts
•within several hours of delivery, the cervix has reformed –
by 1wk it is about 1cm in diameter
round-shaped nulliparous cervix permanently replaced by transverse, fish mouth-shaped external os
– result of laceration & dilation during delivery
•vulvar & vaginal tissues return to normal over the first several says

ovarian function is suppressed during breastfeeding

begin to rise ~2wks after delivery if breastfeeding is not initiated
•the likelihood of ovulation ↑ as frequency/duration of breastfeeding ↓
Return of the elastic fibers of the skin & the stretched rectus muscle to normal configuration occurs slowly & is aided by exercise
seen on the skin during pregnancy (usually lighten in time)
separation of the rectus muscles & fascia
Pregnancy-related cardiovascular changes return to normal 2-3wks after delivery
– primarily caused by blood loss at the time of delivery
•significant shift of extracellular fluid into the intravascular space
seen during pregnancy persists into first several hours of postpartum period
also seen during pregnancy persists ~1hr after delivery, but then decreases
*these cardiovascular events may contribute to the decompensation that sometimes occurs in the early postpartum period in pts w/ heart disease
~5kg of weight is lost as a result of diuresis & the loss of extravascular fluid
•further weight loss varied in weight & amount from pt to pt
persists into the early puerperium for several days
, thus minimizing the usefulness of identifying early postpartum infection by laboratory evidence of a mild-to-moderate elevation in the white cell count
autotransfusion of red cells to the intravascular space
after delivery as the uterus contracts
•remains elevated in the first few weeks postpartum, then returns to normal –
this means drugs w/ renal excretion should be given in increased doses during this time
